subject: GranitePay RFP: vulnerability management technical package & remediation timeline
messages:
From: Eli Morgan <eli.morgan@granitepay.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: nadia.ruiz@granitepay.com
Date: 2026-10-29T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: RFP follow-up: vulnerability management artifacts we need

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the greenlight to include Redwood as part of our vendor shortlist. As part of our security review we need a single deliverable that contains:
- SAST and DAST tooling and coverage (languages, frameworks, pipeline integration)
- Patch SLAs by severity and typical time-to-fix for Redwood-managed components
- Recent pen test executive summary (scope, high/critical findings, mitigations)
- SBOM in machine-readable format (prefer CycloneDX)
- Any third-party dependencies and mitigation controls

Can you provide a technical package and an estimate for how quickly you can commit to remediation SLAs for critical/high issues discovered during our trial? Also tell us who on your side will own this engagement.

Thanks,
Eli Morgan
Director, Security Engineering
GranitePay

--
Attachment requested: "granitepay-rfp-checklist.xlsx" (not yet provided)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Eli Morgan <eli.morgan@granitepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: vulnerability management artifacts we need

Hi Eli / Nadia,

Appreciate the clear list — attaching a consolidated technical package that covers each item. Quick summary here so you can scan:

- SAST: We run a combination of in-house static analysis checks plus SonarQube and Semgrep at build time. Language coverage: Python, Go, Java, TypeScript. Results feed into our CI pipeline; critical findings open an auto-created JIRA ticket for engineering triage.
- DAST: Weekly automated scans against our staging cluster (OWASP ZAP) plus authenticated scans monthly. On-demand scans can be triggered by request through our security ops runbook.
- Patch SLAs: Critical (RCE/privilege escalation): initial triage within 4 hours, remediation or mitigations within 72 hours; High: triage within 24 hours, remediation within 7 days; Medium/Low: remediation tracked on standard backlog (30 days typical).
- Pen tests: Third-party pentest performed quarterly; attached is the executive summary (pen-test-summary-2026-09-15.pdf). Notable: 2 high findings from Sept that were remediated; see summary table in the PDF.
- SBOM: Attached as CycloneDX JSON (sbom-cyclonedx-2026-10-28.json). We publish SBOMs per release and can provide continuous access for approved partners.
- Third-party dependencies: inventory is included; we annotate known CVEs and mitigation status.

Attachments included: redwood-vm-technical-package-2026-11-01.pdf, sbom-cyclonedx-2026-10-28.json, pen-test-summary-2026-09-15.pdf, remediation-action-plan-GP-2026-11.xlsx

Owner on our side: Hannah Schmitt, Security Partnerships (cc'd). Karthik (solutions) will coordinate commercial/contractual questions; Marissa (customer success) will own deliverable follow-through if we proceed.

If you want, we can jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the package and agree a remediation SLA commitment for your pilot. Proposed times: Wed or Thu morning PST.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--

Eli — quick note from the commercial side. We can commit to the remediation SLA matrix Hannah outlined for pilot customers under our standard Dedicated contract. If you need firm contract language (SLA exceptions, credits), Marissa and I can draft a clause for the master services agreement.

From: Eli Morgan <eli.morgan@granitepay.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: nadia.ruiz@granitepay.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: vulnerability management artifacts we need

Thanks Hannah and team. A few clarifying questions after a quick review:

1) DAST cadence — can authenticated scans be run against our staging environment on-demand (we would prefer weekly during the test window)?
2) SBOM format — thanks for CycloneDX. Can you also produce SPDX on request? We ingest SPD X natively into our software composition analysis pipeline.
3) Pen-test scope — for procurement we need confirmation that your pen tests include network-attached inference endpoints and the orchestration control plane. The exec summary you provided lists app-layer findings; can you confirm network/control plane was in scope?
4) Remediation evidence — after fix, can you provide proof-of-fix screenshots or re-scan results (ZAP artifacts or Semgrep run output) tied to the Jira ticket?

If you can answer those items and confirm a 72-hour turnaround on critical fixes during the pilot, we can move forward to contract redlines.

Eli

> On Nov 2, 2026, at 8:22 AM, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> > We can commit to the remediation SLA matrix Hannah outlined...

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Eli Morgan <eli.morgan@granitepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: vulnerability management artifacts we need

Eli — answers inline below.

1) DAST cadence and authenticated scans: Yes. We support on-demand authenticated DAST runs against customer-provisioned staging environments. For the pilot we can schedule weekly authenticated ZAP runs and retain raw scan artifacts for 90 days. We will provide the ZAP report and any relevant authenticated session tokens (obfuscated) as part of the remediation evidence bundle.

2) SBOM formats: We can produce both CycloneDX (default) and SPDX on request. I have included a note in the remediation-action-plan spreadsheet indicating how to request SPDX exports and who to contact.

3) Pen-test scope: The September 2026 third-party pen test included: external/edge endpoints (inference public endpoints), internal orchestration control plane (control plane API surface between control-plane components), and container runtime checks on the dedicated GPU nodes. The executive summary omitted some of the lower-severity control-plane findings for brevity; the full report is available under NDA. High-level: two high issues were application layer auth misconfigurations (now closed), one medium finding in a third-party library (CVE-2026-3479) tracked for patching.

4) Remediation evidence: Affirmative. For every remediation we provide:
   - A JIRA ticket reference (INF-1459 or new ticket)
   - Pre/post ZAP report snippets (PDF) or Semgrep run output (JSON)
   - A short remediation note from the engineering owner

Commitment on 72-hour turnaround for critical issues during the 90-day pilot: We commit to the triage and mitigation timeline (initial triage within 4 hours; mitigation path within 72 hours). If a fix requires a coordinated platform patch that needs scheduled downtime, we will provide a documented mitigation and timeline within the 72-hour window.

Next steps:
- Confirm NDA so we can share the full pentest report.
- We will open INF-1459 in JIRA as the canonical remediation tracking task for GranitePay; all artifacts will be attached there.
- Proposed follow-up: Thu 11/05 09:00 PST to walk the package (30 minutes). Does that work?

Best,
Hannah
